author: kevaundray
content:
Was looking at the 33_024 epoch number; is it correct to say that Prysm, Lodestar and Grandine do not enable historical backfill by default?

For reference I was looking at these links:

- Prysm: https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/462e52404e3965fc0ed4bc1bf7717812d9dd3ef7/cmd/beacon-chain/sync/backfill/flags/flags.go#L12

- Lodestar: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/ec596194e2b909e30e3c6b095fb836427af0c4fb/packages/beacon-node/src/sync/options.ts#L42

- Grandine: https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/blob/eaf220e60699cd63d4223ad2481e42fd15f67802/runtime/src/grandine_args.rs#L2027

author: kevaundray
content: implication being that a newly checkpoint synced node will not backfill 4-5 months of blocks

author: kevaundray
content:
Also resurfacing yet again to hear strong opinions: 

From what I can tell; the safety decay for checkpoint sync is 10% (roughly two weeks) but the historical block retention policy uses a safety decay of 100% (roughly 4-5 months)

I don't really see a good rationale for using 100, what were the arguments against just doubling the WSP at a safety decay of 10 for operational purposes?

author: tersec
content:
I want to very carefully say that I'm obviously not speaking for any non-Nimbus clients, but this might be a misleading flag, because Nimbus has one which looks like it too: https://nimbus.guide/trusted-node-sync.html#delay-block-history-backfill

It's might be a question of backfill from checkpoint sync node or backfill from P2P in a background way. This looks like what's happening with Grandine for example? https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/blob/eaf220e60699cd63d4223ad2481e42fd15f67802/p2p/src/block_sync_service.rs#L152-L212

author: kevaundray
content: Thats a good point, that region of code in particular  is guarded by `if back_sync_enabled` so maybe theres another location in the code that backfills without the backfill flag being set

author: tersec
content: Well, and it's specifically tied to checkpoint sync

author: kevaundray
content:
Also if you have any thoughts about this <@654267572107083777> as well as other CL devs that would be great.

Another way to rephrase my understanding of the safety decay constant: at D=10, a node that syncs from a checkpoint within the weak subjectivity period will retain accountable safety of at least 23% of the total active balance. ie 10% of stake could have initiated a long range attack and it would not be slashable because they would have exited already.

If this sounds correct, we get ~0 at D=33, so its unclear to me as to why we would store blocks assuming D=100
